sections.h: What Does GEO Actually Require?
p: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is not a rebranded version of traditional SEO. It focuses on making a brand or professional entity recognizable and verifiable by large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. These models do not index pages the same way Google does. They rely on structured data, entity recognition, consistent citations across authoritative sources, and clear signals about who you are and what you offer. A GEO consultant needs to understand how these models parse information and how to build a digital footprint that an LLM can reliably use.

sections.h: Check Their Methodology and Tools
p: Any credible GEO consultant should be able to describe their process without vague promises. Ask them how they measure AI visibility. Do they use a dedicated platform or tool that tracks mentions and recommendations across multiple LLMs? Or are they relying on manual searches and guesswork? The ability to measure is essential because GEO is still a new field, and results are not always visible in traditional analytics.

For instance, a consultant might use a tool that checks whether a brand is recommended when a specific query is entered into ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini. They should also be able to show how they track changes over time and correlate those changes with the work they did. Without measurement, you cannot evaluate whether the strategy is working.

sections.h: Look for Sector Specific Experience
p: GEO is not a one size fits all service. Different industries have different entity types, different citation sources, and different ways that LLMs retrieve information. A consultant who works primarily with ecommerce brands may not understand the citation landscape for healthcare clinics or real estate agencies in Dubai.

When evaluating a consultant, ask about their experience in your specific sector. For example, a GEO strategy for a car rental company would focus on making sure the brand appears as a verified entity on travel aggregators, review sites, and local directories that LLMs trust. A healthcare clinic would need to ensure its practitioner profiles, licensing information, and patient review data are structured correctly. A real estate developer would need to align its project listings, agent profiles, and property data across multiple platforms.

Look for consultants who can demonstrate sector specific experience through verifiable client work, case studies (with permission), or published examples of entity audits in your industry. This kind of sector specific experience matters because it means the consultant already knows which data sources are relevant and how to fix common entity gaps in that industry.

sections.h: Verify Their Track Record Through Public Signals
p: Instead of relying on a 'leading' list, verify a consultant's track record through public signals that are hard to fake. Look at their LinkedIn profile for consistent activity, relevant endorsements, and a history of working with brands in your sector. Check whether they have published articles, spoken at events, or been cited by other experts in the field. These signals are more reliable than a list compiled by an unknown editor.

You can also check whether the consultant has a verified profile on professional platforms that provide a public record of their work and methodology. A verified profile adds a layer of transparency because it shows that the consultant's identity and expertise have been checked against real data.

sections.h: Ask About Their Understanding of Entity SEO

Entity SEO involves ensuring that your brand name, logo, description, location, contact details, and social profiles are consistent and correctly attributed across the web. It also involves building relationships between your entity and other trusted entities, such as industry associations, review platforms, and media outlets.

Cross platform citation consistency. AI models train on hundreds of thousands of sources. If your business name appears as "ABC Realty" on one directory and "ABC Real Estate" on another, the model treats them as two separate entities. A GEO specialist audits and corrects these inconsistencies across Google Business Profile, industry directories, social platforms and review sites.

Content that answers questions, not just keywords. AI assistants retrieve answers from content that directly addresses user intent. A GEO specialist helps you publish clear, factual content that answers the specific questions your prospects ask. This is different from writing blog posts stuffed with keywords. It is about being the source the AI can cite.

sections.h: How GEO Differs From SEO in Practice
p: The most common mistake businesses make is treating GEO as a one time project. Traditional SEO can improve rankings with a site audit and a few months of link building. GEO requires continuous maintenance because the AI models change how they select sources.

sections.h: What a GEO Specialist Does Not Deliver
p: A reputable GEO specialist will not promise guaranteed recommendations from ChatGPT or a specific number of AI citations. No one controls the AI's training data or its selection logic. What a specialist can promise is a systematic process to improve your odds: better entity clarity, stronger authority signals and consistent monitoring.

sections.h: Five Questions to Ask Before Hiring a GEO Specialist in Dubai
p: The GEO field is unregulated, and anyone can call themselves a specialist. These questions will help you separate real expertise from buzzwords.

A serious specialist will name a specific tool or methodology. They might use Prezlo, a custom script that queries the AI APIs, or a third party monitoring service. If they only talk about Google Search Console and organic traffic, they are doing traditional SEO, not GEO.

Entity disambiguation means making sure the AI knows your brand is distinct from others with similar names. A good specialist will explain how they use schema markup, Wikipedia citations, and consistent naming across platforms to achieve this. If they cannot explain entity disambiguation, they do not understand the core of GEO.

GEO and reputation management overlap. Ask how they address negative signals. A good answer will include monitoring review platforms, responding to feedback and building positive citations on independent sites. If they claim reviews do not matter, they are ignoring a key AI signal.

AI models change their source selection criteria every few months. A GEO specialist should have a monitoring process in place to detect when your visibility drops and a plan to adjust. If they say the work is permanent, they are overselling.

sections.h: How to Verify a GEO Specialist's Credentials
p: Credentials in this field are limited. A certification from an online course shows foundational knowledge but does not prove practical experience. What matters more is demonstrated expertise. Look for:

Industry recognition. Has the specialist been cited by other experts or featured in industry analysis? For example, a perspective on the shift from optimizing pages to optimizing entities was cited by JC Chouinard in his write up of Google Search Central Live Toronto. That kind of peer recognition is a signal of genuine expertise.

Active presence in the community. Are they active on LinkedIn, GitHub or industry forums? Engagement with peers and ongoing learning suggests they are keeping up with changes. Professional profiles on LinkedIn can show relevant activity.

sections.h: Summary: Separate the Real from the Hype
p: Generative engine optimization is not a magic switch. It is a disciplined process of making your brand easier for AI to find, verify and recommend. A genuine GEO specialist in Dubai will talk about entity structure, citation consistency, authority monitoring and measurement tools. They will not promise guaranteed recommendations or fixed timelines. They will show you case studies and explain their methodology in detail.

If you are evaluating a consultant, start with the five questions above. The answers will tell you whether you are talking to someone who understands the new landscape or someone who is just rebranding old SEO tactics.

sections.h: How AI Visibility Consulting Differs From Traditional SEO
